explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/692, which reports Cambie's computation δ_1(3,6) = 0.35, δ_1(3,7) ≈ 0.33, δ_1(3,8) ≈ 0.3619, where δ_1(n,m) is the density of integers with exactly one divisor in the open interval (n,m). `exactlyOneDivisorIn n m` uses `Set.Ioo n m` and `ncard = 1`, and `IsDelta₁` is `HasDensity`. I recomputed the densities exactly over one period (lcm of the candidate divisors): δ_1(3,6) = 7/20, δ_1(3,7) = 1/3, δ_1(3,8) = 38/105 ≈ 0.3619, so δ(3,7) < δ(3,6) and δ(3,7) < δ(3,8) as stated. The universally quantified δ with the hypothesis that it gives the density for all (a, b) is not vacuous, since each such set is periodic and has a density.
